newsitem.title: USA: Lott says U.S. balanced budget amendment may pass.
newsitem.headline: Lott says U.S. balanced budget amendment may pass.

text.p: Senate Majority Leader Trent Lott said Republicans may have enough votes to pass a balanced budget amendment to the U.S. Constitution during the next session of Congress.

Speaking the morning after the Nov. 5 election, which saw Republicans retain control of the Senate and pick up either one or two seats depending on the outcome of a close Oregon race, Lott said the Senate would concentrate on budget and tax issues when it convenes next January.
The Senate by one vote last session failed to muster the two-thirds majority needed to pass the amendment. But Lott said "it looks like we might have the votes" to pass it in the Senate next year.
Republicans kept control of the House, but lost some seats. Lott said he had not yet assessed how the closer House margin might affect the outlook for the budget amendment.

Lott said Republicans wanted to work with President Clinton to pass budget and tax legislation. He suggested Congress might approve a smaller package of tax cuts, including a capital gains reduction in the next session while lawmakers held hearings on the possibility of a more sweeping overhaul of the U.S. tax code.
"Republicans have learned to listen. I want to hear waht the American people have to say," Lott said about the possibility of broad tax simplification.

He said Republicans would keep pushing to balance the budget, forecasting deeper spending cuts than were approved last year. But he hedged on entitlement reforms, calling on Clinton to go first to present ideas for reforming the Medicare program of health insurance for the elderly.

Democrats attacked Republicans during the election for their proposed reductions in Medicare, accusing them of trying to gut the program. Lawmakers from both parties have suggested an independent commission to recommend changes to the program to keep it solvent over the long run.
